newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas seeks to smooth over TV tiff with CLT, Frere.
newsitem.headline: Havas seeks to smooth over TV tiff with CLT, Frere.

text.p: French media group Havas, bolstered by a six billion franc asset swap with Generale des Eaux, has started talks in a bid to pacify frayed relations with a key owner of Luxembourg's CLT.

Industry sources said on Friday that Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier had started talks with Belgian businessman Albert Frere in order to clean the slate after a damaging row at the start of 1996 in the course of a European merry-go-round of digital television alliances.

"He has started talks and wants to normalise the relationship with Frere and CLT. But he has not gone out to apologise and make amends. It takes two to tango, either we find common ground or we settle a separation," a company source said.
The parties had fallen out when Havas, Canal Plus and Germany's Bertelsmann in March concluded a digital television alliance pact with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and BSkyB.
The deal infuriated Frere because CLT had been having separate talks with Murdoch and Dauzier had been blocking such a deal as CLT board member.
Later in the year Murdoch left the alliance while Bertelsmann renounced its German digital television plans and concluded a merger deal with CLT bringing in its UFA broadcasting activities.
Meanwhile CLT had joined the Television par Satellite (TPS) digital satellite venture in France with TF1 and France Television, which rivals Canal Plus' CanalSatellite.
Dauzier told a news conference on Thursday that he wanted the Frere-controlled Luxembourg holding company Audiofina to keep its stake in Havas.
Audiofina, which controls Compagnie Luxembourgoise de Telediffusion (CLT), has a 4.1 percent stake in Havas which will slip to 3.3 percent after the deal with Generale des Eaux.
He also said he wanted to close the chapter on the "Franco-French" dispute with Frere and CLT.
The first part of Dauzier's approach is to try to change the status of a holding company called CLMM, which is 70 percent owned by Frere-related companies Electrafina and Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
Ideally, company sources said, unlisted CLMM will be merged with listed Audiofina which will make the Havas stake "more liquid" in the case it wants to seek an exit.
But Havas also has a first right of refusal on part of the shares in the new CLT-UFA merger in a pact with Electrafina and Bertelsmann for if it wanted to increase its role.

In an interview ith the Les Echos newspaper on Friday, Dauzier said that "If discussions are started with Albert Frere on the possibility for us to get access to the liquidity of our stake in CLMM, I would look favourably at an increase of the stake of Albert Frere in Havas."
But he added, "I do not want to predict the future of CLT. One thing is clear, we will not finance two rival projects."
